## Why This Is Asked

This tests precise bit-twiddling with non-trivial masks and no loops, a common optimization pattern.

## Key Concepts

- Mask construction for adjacent-bit swaps
- Two-shift strategy and one return
- Edge cases: 64-bit boundaries, unsigned masking

## Code Example

```c
uint64_t swapAdjacent64(uint64_t n) {
  const uint64_t E = 0x5555555555555555ULL;
  const uint64_t O = 0xAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAULL;
  return ((n & E) << 1) | ((n & O) >> 1);
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you generalize to swap every 3-bit group? 
- What are the performance implications on modern CPUs?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to compose bit-fields into a compact word, a common protocol task.

## Key Concepts
- Bit masking
- Bit shifts
- Width enforcement

## Code Example
```javascript
// C-like pseudocode for clarity
uint32_t packHeader(uint8_t version, uint8_t type, uint32_t length) {
  return ((uint32_t)(version & 0xF) << 28) | ((uint32_t)(type & 0xFF) << 20) | (length & 0xFFFFF);
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you validate inputs without branching?
- How would you extend to 64-bit headers with more fields?
